reader.requirement: At 1985 a 66-level entry RENAMES data-name-2 without THROUGH must carry every data attribute of data-name-2 (class/category, PICTURE including scaling P and V, USAGE COMPUTATIONAL, SIGN LEADING/TRAILING SEPARATE, JUSTIFIED, BLANK WHEN ZERO, group-ness) and occupy its storage, for data-name-2 elementary or group, in Working-Storage or a file record.

edition-consulted.switches: ClauseOperandsTakeImplicitQualifiers (Edition.DialectLevel >= 2002): below 2002 data-name-2 is looked up across the whole scope (no implicit qualification) and must be in the record; affects name resolution only, not the attributes forwarded

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry in ResolveRedefinesPass.cs, PlaceBuilder.cs#PlaceForRenames and ReferenceResolver: the only edition switch on this path is RegionClauseCandidates; the attribute forwarding (ren.Pic = From.Pic; PlaceForRenames forwards to data-name-2's place with DenotesAs = alias) is edition-blind.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the attribute/storage forwarding is the same code at 85 and 2023; only operand lookup (implicit qualifiers, 2002+) differs

reader.notes: The no-THROUGH alias forwards to data-name-2's place (PlaceForRenames), so every statement sees data-name-2's description and storage; only the identity (DenotesAs) stays the alias's. Probes across COMP, SIGN SEPARATE, BLANK WHEN ZERO, JUSTIFIED, P scaling, groups, FD records all behave as the renamed item.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR1-SR8 and VI.5.11.4 GR2. Probe rr1.cob (rr1-003) tried operand classes the reader did not: a USAGE INDEX item (SET RIX TO TI, SET TI TO RIX, SET K TO TI gave K=03 and K2=04), an alphabetic item (the class test on 'ab1' gave AL-NOT), a group that contains an OCCURS table (MOVE to the alias, then TE(2)=BB), the subject of a REDEFINES (RDN=12X) and a signed item (NN-NEG, MOVE gave N3=005). rr2.cob and its control rr2b.cob, which uses the original names, drew the same refusals for the alias as for data-name-2: COBOL0819 for MOVE 5 to the alphabetic item and COBOL0809 for MOVE of the index item. So the alias carries the class and category of data-name-2, including the refusals. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.11.4 GR2 (the text is in GR2).
